findings.title: Task 1.1 would add a second BoundsPolicy and break WRAP/REFLECT dispatch
findings.description: The enum already exists at config.py:17–23 with four members (`OPEN`, `WRAP`, `REFLECT`, `SOFT`). Task 1.1 (task file lines 46–55) says to define a three-member `BoundsPolicy` "before WorldBoundsConfig". That adds a second module-level class that shadows the first and drops `SOFT`. `bounds_enforcement.py:41` (`case BoundsPolicy.SOFT:`) would then raise AttributeError. A `match` tests cases in order, so WRAP and REFLECT calls reach that line and fail too. The SOFT branch at config.py:213–219 and the SOFT tests at tests/test_config.py:242–328 would also break.

findings.title: Most planned work already exists; the plan describes a pre-313 tree
findings.description:
Verified against the tree:
- Task 1.2: `policy` is at config.py:52, and `soft_bounds` (line 53) is not mentioned.
- Task 1.3: policy and SOFT loading are at config.py:198–248. The plan puts `_validate_world_bounds` at "around line 156" (task line 69); it is at config.py:180.
- Task 1.4: all six named tests and the round-trip test exist at tests/test_config.py:172–219.
- Tasks 2.1–2.3: bounds_enforcement.py and tests/test_bounds_enforcement.py (20 tests) exist.
- Tasks 3.1–3.2: `world_bounds` is at simulation.py:64, `_bounds_policy` at :76, and the gate at :112–119.
- Task 3.3: server.py:130 passes `world_bounds`, and server.py:134–137 logs the policy.
- Tasks 4.1–4.2: `policy: wrap` is at config/default.yaml:12 and config/test.yaml:12.
- Task 5.3: both frontmatters say `status: complete` (task file line 9, slice line 10), and architecture line 43 is already `[x]`.
- Task 5.4: CHANGELOG.md:27–33 and :42 already have the slice 313 entries.

findings.title: Task 3.1 asks for a required `world_bounds`, but the code makes it optional
findings.description: The signature is `world_bounds: WorldBoundsConfig | None = None` with a fallback to `entity_manager.world_bounds` (simulation.py:73–76). Current constructions without it do not fail. Making it required would mean editing the 20 `SimulationManager(` calls in tests/test_simulation.py (lines 137–565) that pass no `world_bounds`. The claim at task line 233 that they "will fail otherwise" is false for the current signature.

findings.title: Task 5.4 would duplicate CHANGELOG entries
findings.description: Lines 27–33 and 42 already contain the 313 entries. Adding the bullets at task lines 318–320 creates duplicates.

findings.title: The Task 3.4 flip test cannot pass as specified
findings.description: The plan places an agent at (99, 50) with velocity (10, 0), steps once, and asserts `vx < 0`, without setting dt or max_speed. The existing fixture uses `_profile()` with `max_speed=5.0` (tests/test_simulation.py:86–95) and `dt=0.05` (for example line 142). The engine clamps speed before integrating (src/migratory/engine/integration.py:39, 43, 47–73), so vx becomes 5 and x becomes 99 + 5×0.05 = 99.25. No edge is crossed, so vx stays positive. Starting at x=99.9 with the fixture values gives 100.15, which crosses the edge. The test should say so.

findings.title: `np.mod` can return `width` for tiny negative inputs
findings.description: Criterion 7 (slice lines 369–371) and the plan's Task 2.2 note (task line 134) require `[0, width)`. For float64, `np.mod(-1e-15, 100.0)` computes `100 − 1e-15`, which rounds to exactly `100.0`, because the ulp at 100 is about 1.4e-14. That output is outside the half-open interval. This is derived from IEEE rounding and NumPy's remainder implementation, not executed. The existing edge tests (tests/test_bounds_enforcement.py:105–112) use exact values and miss it. Fix: after the mod, set values `>= width` to 0.0 for each axis, and add a `-1e-15` test.

findings.title: Task 5.2 leaves config/test.yaml on a non-default policy with an ambiguous restore
findings.description: Steps 6–7 edit config/test.yaml to `reflect`, then `open`. Step 8 says to restore "whichever policy you want to keep (recommend wrap)", which is not deterministic. If the run is interrupted after Step 6, the file stays on `reflect`, and nothing in the plan detects it. Task 5.5 stages only docs, so the uncommitted edit is left in the tree. Fix: make Step 8 "set `policy: wrap`", add a grep check before Step 4, and state what to do if a previous run was interrupted.

findings.title: Commit markers are checkboxes
findings.description: Lines 96, 179, 249, 286, and 325 use `- [ ] **Commit:** …`. Commit markers must be plain `**Commit**:` lines, not checkboxes.

findings.title: The Task 4.3 commit comes before any test run after the config change
findings.description: Tasks 4.1–4.2 only check that the YAML loads. The first full pytest after the config change is Task 5.1, which runs after this commit. `test_main.py:66–70` starts the server with the default config, and default.yaml now sets `policy: wrap` on a 1000-unit world. The commit is not at a tested point. Add a pytest run to 4.2 before the commit.

findings.title: Frontmatter status and dependencies are wrong before the work is done
findings.description: `status: complete` (line 9) is set before Section 5 runs, which makes Task 5.3 a no-op. Dependencies (line 6) list only 302 and 303. The plan relies on 308 (the "Forces wired" log that Task 3.3 anchors to, server.py:117–121) and on 309 (the pattern Task 3.5 cites, and the slice's cross-slice note at slice lines 335–336). Set `status` to in-progress until 5.3, and add 308 and 309.

findings.title: Notes says SOFT is deferred, but it has shipped
findings.description: The Notes say SOFT is "intentionally deferred" and that adding it later is "purely additive". SOFT is in the enum (config.py:23), is a no-op in `apply_bounds_policy` (bounds_enforcement.py:41–42), and is wired through `force_builder` by slice 314 (CHANGELOG.md:15–26). The three-variant framing in the Context Summary (task lines 18–20) is stale for the same reason.

findings.title: Several line numbers and class names in the plan are wrong
findings.description: Task 1.1 says `WorldBoundsConfig` is at "line 25"; it is at config.py:46–53. Task 1.3 puts `_validate_world_bounds` at "around line 156" (task line 69); it is at config.py:180. Task 1.4 names a `TestWorldBounds` class that does not exist; the tests are in `TestRangeValidation` (tests/test_config.py:139).

findings.title: The plan only partly covers round-trip serialization
findings.description: Task 1.4's round-trip test passes because `config_to_yaml` runs `_serialize_for_yaml` (config.py:657–681), which converts StrEnum to its value. The plan never mentions that function. If someone rewrites `config_to_yaml` from the plan, the round-trip test (test_config.py:207–219) is the only thing that catches the break.

findings.title: Task 3.2 claims zero import-time overhead, but the import is at module top
findings.description: simulation.py:10 imports `apply_bounds_policy` at load time, so that cost is always paid. The Notes at line 329 say no import is avoided. Keep the existing top-level import and drop "import-time" from the check.

findings.title: Task 2.1's required comment is missing
findings.description: Task 2.1 (line 124) asks for a comment referencing `build_world_bounds` in simulation.py. The `_apply_wrap` docstring says the origin is (0, 0) but does not reference `build_world_bounds`.

findings.title: Task 3.5 cites the wrong call-site files
findings.description: tests/test_clients.py constructs no SimulationManager. tests/test_force_builder.py:201–207 and tests/test_repulsor_integration.py:53–59 already pass `world_bounds`. The "Files touched" list (lines 30–40) omits the docs and any test file that Task 3.5 might edit.

findings.title: Manual viewer checks cannot be performed by an agent
findings.description: Step 5 needs a Three.js viewer, 30–60 seconds of watching, and visual judgment. Criterion 14 (slice lines 390–392) depends on it. The plan should name who performs the check, or add an automatable proxy such as a short WebSocket client that asserts snapshot positions stay in bounds, and record the result.

findings.title: Criteria 10 and 11 have no tests in the tree yet
findings.description: No bounds-policy test exists in this file. Task 3.4 is the only place these criteria are covered, so it has to be fixed (see the flip-test finding above) before it can serve as the coverage.

findings.title: Task 5.1 repeats Step 2 of Task 5.2, and the plan is heavier than the slice needs
findings.description: There are 23 task entries for a 2/5 slice that is mostly done, including five one-line commit tasks. Task 5.1 runs the same pytest as Task 5.2 Step 2 (task line 300). Fold 5.1 into 5.2, and fold 4.3 into 4.2 so the commit follows a passing run.

findings.title: Config loader meets criteria 2–5
findings.description: A missing key defaults to OPEN (198–200), matching is case-insensitive (204), the error lists the valid options (206–210), and the round trip works through `_serialize_for_yaml` (657–681).

findings.title: Step gate and dispatch match criterion 10
findings.description: The gate runs only when the policy is not OPEN. It passes `[:count]` views and runs after `tick` (simulation.py:103–119). The mock target `migratory_server.simulation.apply_bounds_policy` exists, because the function is imported by name at simulation.py:10.

findings.title: Enforcement unit tests cover criteria 6–9
findings.description: The 20 tests cover OPEN no-op, WRAP single, large, negative, edge, velocity, and both-axis cases, and REFLECT clamp, flip, and corner cases, matching the Task 2.3 list. The only gap is the float-edge case noted above.
